title: Preserving Heritage and Identity after Merger of Schools
what_it_is: Preserving Heritage and Identity after Merger of Schools

sections.label: Merged school identity building
sections.summary: Merged schools display heritage, unify around common values and symbols, and organise shared experiences to forge new identities over time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The history, traditions and values of the merging schools are displayed in a heritage space or retained in artefacts, such as the school mascot.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Newly merged schools seek to forge new identities by unifying their school community around common values, songs and symbols such as the school crest.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Common experiences, such as cohort camps and schoolwide events, are organised to build collective memories among the students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The forging of a new identity takes time and is an ongoing process for the newly merged schools.

sections.label: Preserving defunct schools' heritage
sections.summary: For defunct schools, heritage components deemed worthy of preserving are captured and retained with stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: For such situations, we look at what are the heritage components of the schools that have gone defunct, that need to be preserved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: As far as possible, we will work with the stakeholders to capture and retain these heritage qualities that are deemed to be worthy of preserving.
